close_reason: Fixed in bf895d2: added 'Field semantics' section to ContactCardFilterCondition distinguishing exact-match, range, and text-match field classes; flagged text-match semantics as server-defined per RFC 9610 §3.3.1, with portability warning that callers SHOULD treat text-match as approximate full-text-search filters, not exact value tests.
description:
ContactCardFilterCondition exposes 11 text-match fields whose doc
comments describe what each field matches against in the data model but
do NOT describe the matching semantics:

- text, name, name_given, name_surname, name_surname2
- nickname, organization
- email, phone, online_service
- address, note

For each, the open question is:
- Case-sensitive vs case-insensitive?
- Substring vs prefix vs exact?
- Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD)?
- Accent folding (Á matches a)?
- Word-boundary vs raw-substring?

RFC 9610 §3.3.1 leaves matching semantics to the server. The wire-types
crate cannot pin them. But the doc comments give a false sense of
portability — "Matches any NameComponent value" implies "any caller can
write portable code that filters by name."

Real-world consequence: server A (e.g. Stalwart) does case-insensitive
NFC-normalized substring match; server B (e.g. Cyrus) does exact-case
NFD substring match; a caller writing
`filter.name = Some("müller".into())` gets different result sets from
identical queries. The wire-types crate has no way to detect this.

Distinction to preserve:
- "exactly equal to" filters (RFC 9610 §3.3.1: `uid`, `kind`,
  `inAddressBook`, `hasMember`) — semantics are fully spec-defined.
- "text-matches" filters (RFC 9610 §3.3.1: text, name, email, etc.) —
  semantics are server-defined.

Minimum fix: add a rustdoc clause to `ContactCardFilterCondition`
explaining the distinction and stating that text-match semantics are
server-defined; portable code MUST NOT assume case-folding, Unicode
normalization, or accent handling.

Stronger fix: per-field annotation marking each as "exact" or
"server-defined match". Adds rustdoc-doctest-verifiable structure.

Cross-reference:
- RFC 9610 §3.3.1 "Filtering" prose, especially the "Matches X if Y"
  vs "Equal to X if Y" phrasings.
- card.rs:188-307 (the FilterCondition struct).
title: ContactCardFilterCondition text-match fields have undocumented matching semantics (server-defined)
